translations.text: The Book of Ezra the Scribe, who is called Shealtiel.
In the thirtieth year after the fall of our city, I, Shealtiel, who am Ezra, was in Babylon. I was lying on my bed, troubled, and thoughts arose in my heart.
because I saw the desolation of Zion and the prosperity of the inhabitants of Babylon.
My spirit was greatly astonished, and I began to speak forceful words to the Most High.
I said, “O Lord, my Lord, did you not speak at the beginning, when you formed the earth, doing this alone, and commanded the dust,
and it gave you Adam, a lifeless body? He was the work of your hands, and you breathed into him the breath of life, and he became alive before you.
You brought him into the paradise that your right hand had planted before the earth came into being.
You gave him a commandment, and he transgressed it. Immediately you decreed death for him and his descendants. From him were born peoples and tribes, languages and nations and families beyond number.
All the peoples went their own ways in their deeds, acting wickedly and unjustly before you, and you did not restrain them.
Then, in time, you brought a flood upon the earth and upon the inhabitants of the world, and you destroyed them.
Their destruction came all at once. Just as death came to Adam, so death through the flood came to them.
But you left one of them alive with his household, and all the righteous descended from him.
When the inhabitants of the earth began to multiply, they increased in children, peoples, and many multitudes, and again began to act more wickedly than those before them.
And when they acted wickedly before you, you chose for yourself one of them whose name was Abraham.
You loved him and showed him the end of the ages, to him alone, privately between you and him, at night.
You established everlasting covenants with him and told him that you would never abandon his descendants. You gave him Isaac, and to Isaac you gave Jacob and Esau.
You chose Jacob as your own inheritance, but you hated Esau, and Jacob became a great people.
When you brought his descendants up from Egypt, you established everlasting covenants with them and brought them to Mount Sinai.
You bent down the heavens and shook the earth. You made the world tremble, caused the depths to quake, and shook the worlds.
Your glory passed through four gates—of fire, earthquakes, wind, and frost—to give the law to Jacob’s descendants and commandments to the people of Israel.
Yet you did not remove the evil heart from them so that your law might bear fruit among them.
For the first Adam clothed himself with an evil heart, transgressed, and was overcome, as were all those born from him.
The affliction remained in them, and the law was in the people’s heart along with the evil root. Then what was good departed, and what was evil came.
Times passed and seasons came to an end. Then you raised up for yourself a servant whose name was David.
You told him to build a city for your name and a house in which offerings from what belongs to you would be presented to you.
This continued for many years, and the inhabitants of the city sinned against you.
They did nothing new beyond what Adam and all his descendants had done, for they too were clothed with an evil heart.
You handed your city over to your enemies.
Then I said in my heart, ‘Perhaps the inhabitants of Babylon act rightly, and for this reason you have abandoned Zion.’
But when I came here, I saw countless wicked deeds. I myself have seen many injustices in this thirtieth year, and my heart was shaken,
because I saw how you tolerate sinners and spare the wicked, while you destroyed your people and preserved your enemies.
You have not made known to anyone how your way can be understood. Has Babylon perhaps acted better than Zion?
Or have you known another people better than Israel? Or what tribe has trusted in your covenant as Jacob has?
Yet their reward has not appeared, and their labor has borne no fruit. For I have traveled among the nations and seen that they prosper now, although they do not remember your commandments.
Now weigh our wrongdoing and that of the inhabitants of the world in a balance, and let the tilt of its unbending beam be seen.
Or when have the inhabitants of the world not sinned before you? Or what people has kept your commandments so well?
You can find individual people by name who have kept your commandments, but you cannot find a nation.”
The angel who had been sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered
and said to me, “Your heart has been greatly shaken by this world, yet you have wanted to understand the way of the Most High.”
I answered, “Yes, my lord.” Again he answered me, “I was sent to show you three ways and to set three examples before you.
If you can explain one of them to me, I too will show you the way you long to see, and I will teach you why the heart is evil.”
I answered, “Speak, my lord.” He answered me, “Go and weigh out a weight of fire for me, or measure out a measure of wind for me, or call back for me the day that has passed.”
I said to him, “Who among those born can do these things you have said, that you should ask all these things of me, my lord?”

And he said to me, “If I had asked you, ‘How many storehouses are there in the heart of the sea? How many springs are there at the head of the deep? How many paths are there above the firmament? What are the exits from Sheol? Or what are the roads of Paradise?’
you would have said to me, ‘I have not descended into the deep. Nor have I yet descended into Sheol. Nor have I ever ascended to heaven.’
But now I have not asked you about these things, but about fire, wind, and the day—things you have experienced and without which you cannot exist—and you have told me nothing about them.
He said to me, “You cannot understand the things that have grown up with you.

How, then, can your vessel grasp the way of the Most High? For the way of the Most High was created in what cannot be comprehended. Someone who decays in a world that decays cannot know the way of the one who does not decay.” When I heard these things, I fell on my face.
And I said to him, “It would have been better for us not to have come than, having come, to live in wickedness and suffer without knowing why we suffer.”
He answered me, “The forests of trees on the plain went out and devised a plan.
And they said, “Come, let us go and wage war against the sea, so that it will retreat before us and we can make another forest for ourselves.”
The waves of the sea likewise formed a plan and said, “Come, let us go up and wage war against the forest of the plain, so that we too can make another place for ourselves there.”
But the forest’s plan came to nothing, for fire came and consumed it.
Likewise, the plan of the waves of the sea came to nothing, for the sand stood firm and restrained them.
“If, then, you were their judge, which of them would you acquit, and which would you condemn?”
I answered and said, “Both of them have devised a futile plan. For the land was given to the forest, and the sea’s place was given to bear its waves.”
He answered and said to me, “You have judged well. Why, then, have you not judged yourself?”

“For just as the land is given to the forest, and the sea’s place to bear its waves, so those who live on earth can know only what is on earth, and the one who is above heaven can know what is above heaven.”
I answered and said, “I ask you, my lord: why, my lord, was I given understanding with which to think?”

“For I did not wish to ask about the ways above, but about the things that happen to us every day: why Israel has been handed over to the nations, and the people you loved have been handed over to wicked tribes; why the holy law of our ancestors has been abolished, and the covenants that were written no longer exist.
We pass from the world like locusts, and our lives are like a breath. We are not even worthy of being shown mercy.”
“But what will he do for his great name, which has been invoked over us? These are the things I asked about.”
He answered and said to me, “If you remain alive, you will see; and if you live long, you will marvel, because the world is hurrying to pass away.
For it cannot bear what has been promised to the righteous, because this world is full of groans and many afflictions.
“For the evil you asked me about has been sown, but its harvest has not yet come.”
Unless, then, what was sown is harvested and the place where evil was sown passes away, the land where good was sown will not come.
For a single grain of evil seed was sown in Adam’s heart from the beginning. How much fruit of wickedness it has produced until now, and will continue to produce until the harvest comes!
Consider this for yourself, then, and see how much fruit of wickedness a single grain of evil seed that was sown has produced.
When, then, the countless [?] of good things are sown, what a harvest they will produce!”
I answered and said, “How long will it be, and when will these things happen? For our years are few and evil.”
He answered and said to me, “You are not in a greater hurry than the Most High. For you are in a hurry for your own sake, but the Most High for the sake of many.
Was it not about these things that the souls of the righteous were asking in their storehouses, saying, ‘How long are we to remain here, and when will the harvest of our reward come?’
The angel Ramiel answered and said to them, ‘Until the number of those like you is complete. For the Holy One has weighed the world.
He has measured the times and counted the seasons. He will neither rest nor stir until the stated number is complete.’”
I answered and said, “O Lord, my lord, but look: we are all full of wickedness.”
“Could it be that the reward of the righteous will be held back because of us, because of the sins of those who inhabit the earth?”
He answered and said to me, “Go and ask a pregnant woman whether, when her nine months are complete, her womb can still hold the child within it.”
I said, “It cannot, my lord.” He answered and said to me, “Sheol and the storehouses of souls are like the womb.”
For just as a woman giving birth is eager to escape the distress of her labor, so these too are eager to give up what was placed in them from the beginning.
“Then the things you long to see will be revealed to you.”
I answered and said, “If I have found mercy in your eyes, and if I am able and worthy—”
Tell me this too: is the time that has passed over us greater, or the time that is yet to come?
For I know the time that has passed, but I do not know what is yet to come.
He answered me, “Stand on the right side, and I will show you the meaning of the parable.”
I stood up and looked, and there before me passed a blazing furnace of fire. When the flame had passed, I looked, and there was smoke left.
After this, a cloud full of water passed before me and poured down a very violent rain. When the violence of the rain had passed, drops remained in it.

He answered me, saying, “Consider within yourself and see: just as the rain is greater than the drops, and the fire than the smoke, so the measure of time that has passed is greater. What remains is drops and smoke.”
I asked him, “Will I really live until those days? Or who will be alive in those days?”
He answered me, “As for the signs you asked me about, I can tell you some of them. But I was not sent to tell you about your life, for I do not know either.”
“As for the signs, look, days are coming when the inhabitants of the world will be seized with great bewilderment. The portion of truth will be hidden, and the land of faith will be barren.
Wickedness and shamelessness will increase beyond what you have now seen and beyond what you heard long ago.
This land that you now see ruling will not endure and will lie untrodden, and people will see this land desolate.
But if the Most High grants you a vision, you will see it thrown into turmoil after the third. Suddenly the sun will appear at night, and the moon during the day.
“Wood will drip blood, stone will raise its voice, nations will be shaken, and the winds will change.
“Someone whom many do not expect will reign, and the birds will migrate.
The Sea of Sodom will produce many fish. One whom many do not know will raise his voice at night, and everyone will hear it.

Chasms will open in many places, and fire will repeatedly be sent out. Wild animals will leave their own regions, and signs will appear through women, for babies will be born before they are fully developed.
Salt water will be found in fresh water, and friends will suddenly wage war against their friends. Then wisdom will be hidden, and understanding will withdraw into its storehouses.
“It will be sought among many but will not be found. Oppression and lawlessness will increase on the earth.
One region will ask its neighbor, ‘Has righteousness passed through you, or anyone who practices righteousness?’ But that region will deny it.
At that time people will hope but will not receive; they will grow weary but will not find; they will labor, but their way will not prosper.
These are the signs I was commanded to tell you. But if you pray again and make your request as you have now, and fast for seven days, you will hear things greater than these.”
And I awoke. My body was trembling violently, and my soul was so exhausted that it seemed about to depart.
The angel who was speaking to me took hold of me, strengthened me, and set me on my feet.
On the second night, Phaltiel, the leader of the people, came to me and said, “Where have you been, and why is your face so sad?
“Do you not know that you are the one entrusted with Israel in the place of their captivity?
Get up, then, and eat a little bread, so that you do not abandon them as a shepherd abandons his flock to destructive wolves.”
I said to him, “Go away from me and do not come near me for seven days. Then come to me, and I will tell you something.” When I said this to him, he went away from me.
And I fasted for seven days, sighing and weeping, as the angel Ramiel had commanded me.
After seven days, the thoughts of my heart again began to distress me greatly.
My soul received a spirit of understanding, and I again began to speak before the Most High these words of prayer and supplication.
I spoke and said, “O Lord, my Lord, from all the earth’s woods and trees you chose one vine for yourself.
And from all the lands of the world you chose one place for yourself.

From all the depths of the sea you made one river abundant for yourself. From all the flowers of the world you chose one flower for yourself, and from all the cities that have been built you consecrated Zion for yourself.
From all the birds that were created you named one dove for yourself, and from all the sheep that were created you favored one ewe.
From the multitude of nations you brought one people near to yourself, and you gave the law, chosen above all, to the people you loved.
And now, Lord, why have you handed over the one to the many, and despised the one root more than the many? You have scattered and dispersed your only one among the many.
And those who oppose your commandments have trampled on those who trusted in your covenant.”
But if you truly hated your people, they should have been disciplined by your own hands.
After I had spoken these words, the angel who had been sent to me the previous night was sent to me again.
And he said to me, “Listen to me, Ezra, and I will instruct you. Look at me, and I will set words before you.”
I answered him, “Speak, my lord.” He said to me, “You have been greatly disturbed over Israel. Or do you love him more than his Maker does?”
I said, “No, my lord. Rather, I spoke out of anguish, because my innermost parts torment me constantly. I want to understand the decree of the Most High and investigate something of his judgment.”

He said to me, “You cannot.” I said to him, “Why, my lord, do I pray? Or why was I born? Why did my mother’s womb not become my grave, so that I would not see Jacob’s suffering and the distress of Israel’s descendants?”
He answered me, “Count for me those who have not yet come. Gather for me the drops that have been scattered, and make the withered flowers green again.

Open for me the storehouses that are locked, and bring out for me the winds imprisoned in them. Show me the likeness of faces you have not yet seen, or show me the likeness of a voice. Then I will tell you about the suffering and the time you have sought to see.”
I said, “O Lord, my lord, who can know these things except someone who does not live among human beings?”
But I am foolish and wretched. How can I speak about the things you have asked me?”
He said to me, “Just as you cannot do a single one of the things mentioned, so you cannot discover my judgment or the fulfillment of the love I promised my people.”
I said, “But, my lord, you have made your promise to those who are at the end. What will those before us do, or we ourselves, or those after us?”
He answered me, “I have likened my judgment to a wreath: just as those at the end have no delay, so those at the beginning have no head start.”
I answered, “Could you not have made those who have been, those who are, and those who will be all at once, so that you could make your judgment known quickly?”
He answered me, “Creation cannot hurry ahead of its Creator. Otherwise, the world could not have borne those who would have come into being in it all at once.”

Again I answered, “Then how did you tell your servant that you would bring back to life, all at once, the creation you made? If, then, they will come to life all at once and creation can bear them, it could also now have borne those coming into being all at once.”
He answered me, “Ask a woman’s womb and say to it, ‘If you give birth to ten children, why do you give birth to them at different times?’ Then ask it to deliver all ten of them.
And I said, “She cannot, my lord, except at intervals.”
And he said to me, “I too have made the earth a womb for those who come upon it at intervals.
For just as a young child cannot give birth, nor can a woman who has grown old give birth again, so I have ordered the world that I created.”
I asked him, “Now that you have given me an opening, I will speak before you. Our mother Zion, about whom you spoke to me—is she still young, my lord, or is she already nearing old age?”
And he answered me, “Ask a woman who gives birth, and she will tell you.
“Say to her, ‘Why do those you now bear resemble the earlier ones, yet are smaller in stature?’
She herself will tell you, ‘Those born in the strength of youth are one thing, and those born in old age, when the womb weakens, are another.’
Look for yourself and see that you are smaller in stature than those who came before you.
Those who come after you will also be smaller still than you, because creation has already grown old, and the vigor of its youth has passed away.”
I answered, “I ask you, my lord, if I have found favor before you, tell your servant through whom you will attend to your creation.”

He answered me, “At first, through a human being, but the end will be by my own hands. For before the earth of the inhabited world existed, before the world’s outlets were established, and before the masses of the winds began to blow,
before the sound of thunder was heard, before the flashes of lightning shone, and before the ground of Paradise was made firm,
before the beauty of the flowers appeared, before the force of earthquakes gained strength, and before the countless armies of angels were gathered,
before the heights of the air were raised, before the expanses of the heavens were named, and before Zion’s footstool was established,
before the present years were examined, before the offenses of those who now sin were formed, and before those who stored up treasures of faithfulness for themselves were sealed,
Then I planned, and all these things came into being through my hands alone, and not through the hands of another.
I answered and said, “What is the division between the ages? When is the end of the first age, and what is the beginning of the second?”
He answered and said to me, “From Abraham to Abraham. Isaac was born to Abraham, and Jacob and Esau were born to Isaac. Jacob’s hand was holding Esau’s heel.
The heel belongs to the first, Esau, and the hand to the second, Jacob.
For a person’s beginning is his hand, and a person’s end is his heel. So do not seek anything else between the heel and the hand, Ezra.”
And I answered, “O Lord, my lord, if I have found favor in your eyes,
“Make known to me, your servant, the completion of these signs, about which you told me a little last night.”
And he answered me, “Stand on your feet, and you will hear a loud voice.
And if the place where you are standing should shake violently
“When you are being spoken to, do not be frightened, for the message concerns the good that comes at the end, and the foundations of the earth will be understood.”
The word concerns them, and they are alarmed and shaken, for they perceive that their end is changing.
When I heard this, I stood on my feet. I listened, and there was a voice speaking, and its sound was like the sound of many waters.
He said, “Look, the days are coming, and when I draw near to visit the inhabitants of the earth,
and when I am about to call the wicked to account for what their hands have done, and when Zion’s humiliation comes to an end,
“When this world, which is destined to pass away, is about to be brought to its close, I will perform these signs: books will be opened across the sky, and everyone will see my judgment together.
One-year-old children will speak and make their voices heard. Pregnant women will give birth before their time, to children at three or four months, and they will live and leap about.
Suddenly, places that have not been sown will be found sown, and storehouses that are full will suddenly be found empty.
A horn will sound loudly, and everyone will suddenly hear it and be terrified.
At that time friends will fight against their friends like enemies, so that the earth and its inhabitants will be astonished. The outlets of springs will stop flowing for three hours.
Whoever survives all these things that I have already told you about will live and see my salvation and the end of the world.
Then he will see those people who were taken up, who have not tasted death since their birth. The hearts of the earth’s inhabitants will be transformed and changed to a different understanding.
For evil will be forgotten, and deceit will be extinguished.
Faith will blossom, corruption will be defeated, and truth, which remained without fruit for many years, will be revealed.”
While he was speaking with me, the place where I was standing began to shake little by little.
And he said to me, “These are the things I have come to make known to you tonight.”
“If, then, you seek again and fast for seven days, I will reveal to you still greater things than these.
“For your voice has indeed been heard by the Most High. The Mighty One has seen your innocence, and also the holiness that you have had since your youth.
For this reason he sent me to reveal all these things to you.” And he said to me, “Take courage and do not be afraid.
Do not be hasty in dwelling on the evils of former times, so that punishment may not come upon you in the last times.”
After these things, I wept and fasted for seven days, to complete the three weeks that had been prescribed for me.
On the eighth night, my heart was again troubled within me, and I began to speak before the Most High.
because my spirit was seething intensely, and my soul was aflame.
I said, “O Lord, my Lord, you spoke at the beginning of your creation, on the first day. You commanded heaven and earth to come into being, and your word, my Lord, accomplished the work.
Then the Spirit was hovering, darkness was covering everything, and there was silence, without a sound. There was not yet any human voice.
Then you commanded the radiance of light to come out of your own storehouses, so that your works might be seen.
On the second day, you created the spirit of the firmament and commanded it to make a division between the waters, so that one part of them would rise above and the other part would remain below.

On the third day, you commanded the waters to gather into one of the earth’s seven parts. You dried out and preserved the other six parts, so that some of them might serve before you and be cultivated and sown.
Your own word went out, and immediately the work was done.

For then, suddenly, countless fruits sprouted, sweet to taste in every variety, along with flowers unlike one another in appearance, trees whose appearance cannot be compared, and aromatic plants whose fragrances cannot be fathomed. These things came into being on the third day.
On the fourth day you commanded, and there came into being the shining sun, the radiance of the moon, and the ordered array of stars.
You commanded them to serve the human being who was to be formed by you.
On the fifth day you commanded the seventh part, where the waters were, to bring forth animals, birds, and fish.
And the waters, which cannot speak and have no life, were producing living things, so that from these the generations might recount your wonders.
Then you kept two creatures that you had created. You named one Behemoth, and you named the other Leviathan.
You separated them from one another, because that seventh part, the watery region, could not hold them both.
You gave Behemoth one of the parts that you had dried up on the third day, to live there, where there are a thousand mountains.
But to Leviathan you gave one of the seven parts of the watery region. You kept them to be food for whomever you wish, whenever you wish.
On the sixth day you commanded the earth to bring forth before you livestock, wild animals, and creeping creatures.
Over these you appointed Adam as ruler over all the works you had created before him. From him we have come, the people you have chosen.
I have said all these things before you, O Lord my Lord, because you said that you created this world for our sake.
But the rest of the nations descended from Adam, you said, are nothing. You compared them to spit, and you compared their abundance to a drop from a bucket.
And now, Lord, look: those nations that were counted as nothing rule over us and trample us.
But we are your people, whom you honored and called your firstborn, your only child, near and dear to you. Yet look, we have been handed over into their hands.
If the world was created for our sake, why do we not inherit our world? How long will these things continue?
After I had finished speaking these words, the angel who had been sent to me on the earlier nights was sent to me again.
He said to me, “Stand up, Ezra, and listen to the words I have come to tell you.”
I said to him, “Speak, my lord.” He answered me, “Suppose a sea lies in a spacious place, broad and boundless.
but its entrance lies in a narrow place, so that it resembles a river.
If someone wishes to enter the sea, see it, and become its master, how can he reach the spacious place unless he passes through the narrow passage?
Listen to another example. There is a city built and situated in a vast plain, and that city is full of many good things.
Its entrance is narrow and set on a height, with fire on the right and deep water on the left.
A single path lies between the two, between the fire and the water, and that path is only wide enough for a person's foot.
If that city is given as an inheritance, how can the heir take possession of his inheritance unless he passes through the danger that lies before him?”
I said to him, “Yes, that is so, my lord.” He answered me, “So it is also with Israel's portion.
For I made the world for their sake, and when Adam transgressed my commandments, what had been made was condemned.
For this reason the entrances to this present world have become narrow, full of sighing, toil, great danger, and severe hardship, together with illnesses and sufferings.
But the entrances to the world to come are spacious and free from anxiety, and they produce fruit that does not perish.
Therefore, unless the living pass through these afflictions and hardships, they cannot obtain the things laid up for them.
Why, then, are you now disturbed, since you are perishable? And why are you troubled, since you are mortal?”
And why have you not taken to heart what is to come, but only what is present?
I answered, “O Lord my Lord, you have clearly stated in your law that the righteous will inherit these things, but the wicked will perish.
So the righteous can well endure afflictions, because they hope to come to a place of relief. But the wicked endure afflictions and never see relief.”
He answered me, “You are not wiser than God, nor do you have more understanding than the Most High.
“Therefore many who have come into being will perish, because they have despised the law established by me.
For God gave a command to those who came into being, when they came into being, telling them what to do so that they might live, and what to observe so that they would not be tormented.
“But they rebelled and did not obey him, and devised empty thoughts for themselves.
But they devised destructive schemes for themselves, and despite all these things they said that the Most High does not exist, and they did not acknowledge his ways.
They despised his law, denied his covenants, did not believe his commandments, and scorned his works.
“Therefore, Ezra, empty things are for the empty, and full things for those who are full.
For look, the days are coming, and when the signs that I previously told you about come, the bride who appears as a city will be revealed, and she who is now set apart will be seen.
“Everyone who escapes these evils foretold long ago will see my wonders.
For my son, the Messiah, will be revealed with those who are with him, and he will bring joy to those who remain for thirty years.
After these years, my son, the Messiah, will die, along with all those who have human breath within them.
The world will return to its original silence for seven days, as it was in the beginning, so that no one remains.
After seven days, that world which is not now awake will be awakened, and corruption will die.
The earth will give up those who lie in it, the dust will give up those who sleep in it, and the storehouses will give up the souls that were placed in them.
The Most High will be revealed on the judgment seat, and the end will come. Mercy will pass away, compassion will withdraw, and patience will be taken away.
“My judgment alone will remain, truth will stand, and faithfulness will rejoice.
“Deeds will come forward, reward will be made known, righteous acts will awaken, and wicked acts will not sleep.
The pit of torment will be seen, and opposite it the place of rest. The furnace of Gehenna will be revealed, and opposite it the paradise of delights.
Then the Most High will say to those nations that are being awakened, “Look and see whom you have denied, whom you have not served, and whose commandments you have rejected.”
“Look, then, in front of you: here are rest and delights, and there are fire and torment.” He will say these things to them on that day of judgment.
For that day of judgment is like this: there is no sun in it, no moon, and no stars;
no clouds, no lightning, no thunder, no winds, no water, no air, no darkness, no evening, and no morning;
no summer, no winter, no beginning of the year, no heat, no ice, no frost, no hail, no dew, and no rain;
no noon, no night, no daytime, no light, no brightness, no radiance, and no splendor, but only the shining of the glory of the Most High, by which they will see what has been prepared.
Its duration will be like a week of years.
This is my judgment and its law, and I have made them known to you alone.
I answered and said, “Lord, my Lord, I said it then, and now I say it again: blessed are all those who have come into being and have kept the commandments laid down by you.
“But concerning those for whom I plead: who among those who have come into being has not sinned? Or who among those born has not transgressed your commandment?
“Now I see that the world to come is destined to bring delight to a few, but torment to many.

“For there is an evil heart within us. It has led us astray from these things, led us to corruption, shown us the ways of death, made known to us the paths of destruction, and distanced us from life. This has happened not to a few, but [?] to all who have come into being.”
He answered and said to me, “Listen to me, Ezra, and I will tell you and instruct you again.
For this reason the Most High made not one world, but two.
As for your saying that the righteous are not many but few, listen to this in reply:
“If you have precious stones, and they are few compared with the number of these, obtain lead and clay for yourself.”
I said, “How is that possible, my lord?”
He answered and said to me, “Not only this, but ask the earth, and it will tell you. Speak to it, and it will explain to you.”
Say to it, ‘You have produced gold, silver, bronze, iron, lead, and clay.
“Silver is more abundant than gold, copper than silver, iron than copper, lead than iron, and clay than lead.”
Compare them, then, and see: which are precious and valuable, the abundant things or the scarce ones?”
I answered and said, “Lord, my Lord, the abundant things are cheap, and the scarce ones are precious.”
He answered and said to me, “Then weigh for yourself what you have thought, because anyone who has a little, a small amount, rejoices in it more than someone who has many things.”
Such is the promise of my judgment. For I rejoice and take pleasure in the few who live, because they are the ones who now uphold my glory, and because of them my name is now glorified.

I am not distressed over the great number of those who perish. For they are the ones who have now become like a breath; they have been counted as smoke and compared to a flame that blazed and went out.
I answered and said, “O earth, what have you done, that these have been born from you and are going to destruction? But if understanding comes from dust, like the rest of creation—
it would have been better if even the dust itself had not existed, so that understanding would not have come from it.
yet now understanding grows with us, and because of this we are tormented, because we perish with full knowledge.
Let the families of humanity mourn, but let the wild animals rejoice. Let all who are born lament, but let the cattle and sheep take pleasure.
For they are far better off than we are, because they do not await judgment or know torment, nor has life after death been promised to them.
For what do we gain by being alive, except that we suffer torment?
For all who are born are entangled in sins and full of wrongdoing, and their transgressions weigh heavily upon them.”
If we did not come to judgment after death, it would have been far better for us.”
He answered and said to me, “When the Most High was making the world, he prepared judgment beforehand for Adam and all who came from him, together with everything belonging to that judgment.
Now understand from your own words, for you said that understanding grows with us.

The inhabitants of the earth are therefore tormented for this reason: although they possessed understanding, they did wrong; they received commandments but did not keep them, and they also rejected the law established for them.
What, then, would they have to say at the judgment? Or how will they open their mouths and speak at the last time?
For how long the Most High has been patient with the inhabitants of the world—not for their own sake, but because of the appointed times!”

I answered and said, “If I have found mercy before you, O Lord, my Lord, make this known to your servant too: after death, when each of us gives up our soul, are we kept at rest until those times come when you will renew your creation, or are we tormented immediately?”
He answered and said to me, “I will tell you about this too. But do not associate yourself with the rebellious, or count yourself among those who are tormented.
For you have a treasure of deeds stored up with the Most High, and it will not be shown to you until the last times.

This is the account concerning death: when the appointed sentence goes out from the Most High for a person to die, as the soul separates from the body to be sent to the one who first gave it, it bows before the glory of God.
But if it belongs to the unjust, or to those who did not keep the ways of the Most High, or to those who hated the people who fear God,
these souls do not enter the storehouses. Instead, they are tormented immediately, groaning and suffering distress in seven ways.
The first way: because they rebelled against the law of the Most High.
The second way: because they cannot return and do good deeds through which they might live.
The third way: because they see the reward stored up for those who believed.

The fourth way: when they know and understand the torment awaiting them at the end, in which the souls of the wicked are punished, because, while they had time to act, they did not submit to the commandments of the Most High.
The fifth way: they see the storehouses of the other souls, which are guarded by angels in great rest.
The sixth way: because they see the torment already prepared for them.

The seventh way, which is greater than all the ways mentioned before: they waste away in shame, are consumed by anguish, and burn with fear as they see the glory of the Most High, against whom they have sinned during their lives, and before whom they will be judged at the end.
But for those who kept the way of the Most High, this is the way when the day comes for them to be released from this perishable vessel.
For during the time they lived in it, they served the Most High with toil and endured danger at all times, because they faithfully kept the law of the one who established the law for them.
Therefore, this is the pronouncement concerning them.
First they see with great joy the glory of the Most High, who leads them. They find rest and proceed in seven ways.
The first way: because they struggled with great toil to overcome the evil inclination formed within them, so that it would not lead them astray from life to death.
The second way: they see the turmoil in which the souls of the wicked are tossed about and battered, and the torment reserved for them.
The third way: they see the testimony that their Maker bears about them, because during their lives they kept the law entrusted to them.

The fourth way: they see and understand the rest they now have when they are gathered into their storehouses. They enjoy great rest and are guarded by angels, and they see the glory reserved for them at the end.

The fifth way: they rejoice at how they have now escaped what is perishable and how they will inherit what is to come. They also see the distress and great toil from which they have been freed, the relief they are to receive, and the delights they will obtain, and they become immortal.
The sixth way: when they are shown how their faces will shine like the sun, and how they will resemble the light of the stars and never perish again.

The seventh way, which is greater than all those mentioned before: they exult openly, take courage, and feel no shame. They eagerly hasten to see the face of the one whom they served during their lives, from whom they will receive glory, and from whom they will receive their reward.

These are the ways that the souls of the righteous can look forward to from now on. But the rebellious will receive from now on the ways of torment mentioned before. These souls do not enter the storehouses, but from now on they are tormented, groaning and mourning in seven ways.
I answered and said, “Then will souls be given room or time, after they leave their bodies, to see what you have told me?”
He answered and said to me, “They have seven days of freedom. During those seven days they see the things mentioned before, and afterward they will be gathered into their storehouses.”

I answered and said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, make this also known to me, your servant: whether on the day of judgment the righteous can make requests for the wicked or plead for them with the Most High,
or fathers for their children, or children for their fathers, or brothers for their brothers, or relatives for their relatives, or friends for their friends.”

He answered and said to me, “Because you have found favor in my eyes, I will tell you about this too. The day of judgment is a decisive day, and it reveals to everyone the seal of truth. Just as now a father does not send his son, or a son his father, or a master his servant, or a friend his loved one, to be sick in his place, or to sleep, eat, or be healed,
so then no one will be able to plead for anyone else on that day, nor will anyone be able to lay a burden on another. For then everyone will bear their own righteousness or wrongdoing.”
I answered and said, “Then how, my lord, do we find that Abraham pleaded long ago for the people of Sodom, and Moses in the wilderness for our ancestors when they sinned,
and Joshua son of Nun after him for Israel in the days of Achan,
and Samuel in the days of Saul, and David over the calamity that struck the people, and Solomon for those in the sanctuary?
and Elijah for those who received rain, and for the dead man so that he might live,
and Hezekiah for the people in the days of Sennacherib, and many others on behalf of many?
If, then, even now, when corruption has become great and wrongdoing has increased, the righteous have pleaded for the wicked, why, my lord, should it not be so then as well?”
He answered and said to me, “This world has an end, and the glory of God does not remain in it continually. For this reason the strong have pleaded for those who have no strength.
But the day of judgment is the end of this world and the beginning of the world to come, which does not die, in which corruption passes away.
Licentiousness is dissolved, unbelief is abolished, righteousness grows, and truth dawns.
Then no one will be able to have mercy on someone condemned in judgment, nor to harm someone acquitted in judgment.”
I answered and said, “This is my first and last word: it would have been better for the earth not to have brought forth Adam, or, after bringing him forth, to have warned him not to sin.
For what benefit is there for all who have come into being? Look, they live in distress, and when they die they await torment.
Oh, what have you done, Adam? Although it was you who sinned, the evil was not yours alone, but ours also, we who have come from you.
For what advantage is there if an undying age has been promised to us, but we have done deeds that bring death?
And an unfailing hope has been made known to us, but we have wickedly been emptied of it?
And treasures free from anxiety and sickness are kept safe, but we ourselves have behaved wickedly?
And if the glory of the Most High is to overshadow those who have lived chastely, but we have walked in evil ways?
And paradise is revealed, whose fruits do not decay, and in which there are delights and healing?
But we do not enter, because we have labored in evil places.
And if the faces of the holy ones are to shine more brightly than the stars, but our faces will be blacker than darkness?”
For during our lives, while we were acting unjustly, we did not consider that we would suffer after our death.”
He answered and said to me, “This is the meaning of the contest that a human being born on earth fights.
“If he is condemned, he will suffer what you have reckoned; but if he is acquitted, he will receive what you have said.

For this is the way Moses spoke of while he was still alive, when he said to the people, “See, today I have set before you life and death, good things and evil things. Choose life, then, so that you and your descendants may live.”
But they rebelled and did not obey him, or the prophets after him, or even me, who spoke with them.
Therefore there will be no sorrow over their destruction, just as there will be joy over the lives of those who have obeyed.
I answered him, “I know, my lord, that the Most High is now called merciful because he has mercy on those who have not yet come into the world;
And gracious, because he shows grace to those who turn to his law;
And patient, because he is patient with us who sin, because we are what he has made;
And generous, because he desires to give rather than to demand;
and abundantly compassionate, because he lavishes compassion all the more on those who exist now, on those who have passed away, and on those who are yet to come;
For if he did not increase his mercies, the world and its inhabitants could not live.
and generous, because unless he gives in his goodness so that the wicked may be relieved of their wickedness, not one in ten thousand human beings could live;
and a judge, because unless he [?] the souls of those who were created by his word and forgets the multitude of their wrongdoings, only a very few would remain out of an innumerable multitude.”
He answered me, “The Most High made this world for many, but the world to come for few.

I will explain the matter to you, Ezra. If you ask the earth, it will tell you which kind of soil it produces in greater abundance: that from which clay is made, or that from which gold is made. Such is the making of this world.
Many have been created, but few will live.”
I answered and said, “Drink in knowledge, my soul, and drink understanding, my heart.
For you came against your will, and you depart unwillingly. Authority has not been given to you, except over a life lasting a short time.”

“O Lord, my Lord, if you permit your servant, I will plead before you that you give us seed and the cultivation of a new heart, from which fruit may come, so that every perishable being who has put on human form may be able to live.
For you are one, and we are one thing you have formed, the work of your hands, as you have said.

Indeed, you give us life, now giving life in the womb to the body you have formed, and assembling its limbs. Your creation is preserved in fire and water, and for nine months the being you have formed bears within her the creature you created.
Both the one who preserves and the one who is preserved are kept safe by your care. And when the womb gives up what has come into being within it,
you commanded milk to come from the limbs themselves, the fruit of full breasts.
so that what was formed may grow for a little while, afterward you guide it in your mercy.
You nourish him in your righteousness, guide him by your law, and instruct him in your wisdom.
You put him to death as your creation, and you give him life as your handiwork.
If, then, you swiftly and easily destroy this being, which was formed at your command with all this great labor, why did it come into being at all?
Now I have spoken about all humanity, but you know that I am especially concerned about your people,
and about your inheritance, over which I mourn, and about Israel, for whom I grieve, and about Jacob’s descendants, for whom I am troubled.
Therefore I will begin to plead and entreat you for myself and for them, for I see the failings of us who dwell in the world.
But now I have also heard the sentence of the coming judgment.
Therefore hear my voice and listen to the words of my prayer, and I will speak before you, Lord my God.
Lord, you who dwell forever, whose heights are exalted and whose dwellings are in the air,
You whose throne is boundless and whose glory is beyond comprehension, before whom the heavenly hosts stand in fear;
at whose word they are changed into fire and wind, whose word is trustworthy and whose utterance endures,
whose command is firm and whose words are fearsome; whose appearance dries up the deep and whose rebuke melts the mountains; whose truth bears witness—
hear the voice of your servant, listen to the plea of the one you formed, and consider my words.
For while I am alive I will speak, and while I still have understanding I will give an answer.
Do not look at the failings of your people, but at those who have served you in truth.
Do not look at the follies of the wicked and their schemes, but at those who kept your covenants amid disgrace.
do not take account of those who have behaved wickedly before you, but remember those who willingly learned to fear you.
Do not desire to destroy those who have become like cattle, but look upon those who have received the light of your law.
Do not be angry with those who have acted worse than wild animals, but love those who have continually put their trust in your glory.
For we and those before us have done destructive deeds and acted wantonly. Yet it is because of us sinners that you have been called merciful.
For if you choose to have mercy on us, who have no deeds, you are called gracious.
For the righteous, whose deeds are stored up with you, have a reward to receive from their own deeds.
For what is a human being that you should be angry with him, or a perishable race that you should be furious with it?
For truly, no one born has been free of wrongdoing, and no one who has lived has been free of sin.
For in this your goodness is made known, O Lord, my Lord: when you have mercy on those who have no strength of good deeds.”
He answered and said to me, “Some of these things you have spoken rightly, and it will be according to your words.
For truly, I am not concerned about the formation of the wicked, or their death, or their judgment, or their destruction.
Rather, I delight in the coming into being of the righteous, in their lives, and in the payment of their reward.
For as you have spoken, so it will be.

For just as a farmer sows many seeds and plants many plants, yet not all the seeds survive in their season, nor do all the plants take root, so too not all those who have come into the world will live.
I answered and said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let me speak before you.
For if the farmer’s seed does not receive your rain at the proper time, can it live? Yet it is also ruined by too much rain.
But the human being who was formed by your hands and made in your likeness, for whose sake you created everything—have you compared him to the farmer’s seed?
No! I beg you, O Lord, my Lord, have pity on your people and show mercy to your inheritance. For it is on your own creatures that you show mercy.
He answered and said to me, “The things of the present are for those who are present, and the things to come are for those who are to come.
For you are far from being able to love my creation more than I do. But you have closely likened yourself to the wicked. Do not let it be so.
But in this too you will be praised before the Most High,
Because you have humbled yourself as you ought, and have not ranked yourself with the righteous, you will therefore be glorified all the more.
For the inhabitants of the world will suffer great misery at the end, in return for the great pride the world displayed.
But you, consider yourself, and seek the glories of those who are like you.

For paradise has been opened for you, the tree of life has been planted, the world to come has been prepared, delight has been made ready, the city has been built, rest has been established, goodness has been perfected, and wisdom has been brought to completion.
The root has been sealed off from you, sickness has died away from you, death has been hidden, Sheol has fled, and corruption has been forgotten.
Pains have been removed from you, and at the end the treasures of life have been revealed.
Therefore, do not ask any further about the many who perish.
For they received freedom and rejected the Most High. They also treated his law with great contempt and disregarded his ways.
They also trampled on his holy ones.
And they said in their hearts that there is no God, although they knew full well that they would die.
Therefore, just as these things spoken of before await you, so thirst and the coming torment await them. For the Most High does not desire human beings to perish.
But those who were created dishonored the name of their Maker, denied his grace, and did not acknowledge me, who prepared life for them,
For this reason my judgment has drawn near,
which I have not made known to the many, but only to you and to the few who are like you.” And I answered and said,
“Now, Lord, you have made known to me the many signs that you are going to perform in the last days, but you have not made known to me at what time.”
He answered and said to me, “Consider it carefully for yourself: when you see that one part of the signs spoken of before has passed,
then understand that this is the time when the Most High is going to visit the world that was made by him.
and when earthquakes in various places, unrest among crowds, treachery among nations, disturbances among rulers, and alarm among leaders appear in the world,
Then it became clear that the Most High had spoken about these things long ago.
for just as everything that happens in the world has a known beginning and an evident end,
so too the times of the Most High: their beginnings are known through signs, wonders, and mighty deeds, and their end through punishment and signs.
And everyone who survives, everyone who is able to escape through his deeds or through the faith with which he has believed,
He will be spared the danger spoken of before and will see my salvation in my land and within my borders, which I have set apart for myself from ancient times.
Then those who now neglect my ways will be astonished, and those who despised and cast them aside will be in torment.
For all those who did not acknowledge me during their lives, while I was doing good to them,
and all those who acted arrogantly against my law, who had freedom,
While an opportunity for patience was open to them, they did not understand but neglected it. They were bound to learn these things after death.
Therefore, from now on, do not investigate how the wicked are tormented. Instead, inquire how the righteous live, those to whom the world belongs and for whose sake the world came into being.”
And I answered and said:
“Even now I say again, and afterward I will say again, that those who perish are more numerous than those who live.”
just as the waves are greater than a little drop.”
He answered me, “As the land is, so are its seeds; as the flowers are, so are their colors; as the worker is, so are the fragrant plants; and as the farmer is, so is the threshing floor.”
For it was in the time of the world, when I was preparing for those who now exist, before there were worlds to inhabit it. No one stood against me, for there was no one.
But now that they have been created in a world made ready, at a table that lacks nothing, and under a law that cannot be fathomed, they have corrupted themselves by their deeds.
I looked at my world, and there it was, ruined; at my inhabited earth, and there it was, in danger because of the conduct of its inhabitants.
I looked and had pity on a very few. I preserved for myself a grape from a cluster and a sapling from a great thicket.
So let the multitude perish, since it has become worthless, but let my grape and my sapling be preserved, which were brought into being with great toil.
But as for you, if you set yourself apart for another seven days, do not fast during them again.
Go to the plain of flowers, where no house has been built. Eat only the flowers of the plain. Taste no meat and drink no wine, but eat only flowers.
Seek the Most High earnestly, and I will come to you and speak with you.
I went, as he commanded me, to the plain called Arpad. I sat there among the flowers of the ground and ate the roots of the field. Eating them satisfied me.
After seven days, while I was lying on the grass, my heart began to be troubled within me again, as before.
My mouth opened, and I began to speak before the Most High. I said:

O Lord, my Lord, you revealed yourself to our ancestors in the wilderness of Sinai when they had come out of Egypt, while they were passing through the wilderness, through a land with no fruit, where no one had passed. You said to them,
You, Israel, listen to me; descendants of Jacob, pay attention to my words.
“Look, I am sowing my law among you, and it will produce fruits of righteousness among you, and through it you will be glorified forever.”

But our ancestors received the law and did not keep it, and the commandments and did not carry them out. Yet they had the fruits of your law, which do not perish, for they could not perish, because it is yours.
But those who received it perished because they did not keep what had been sown in them.
This is the rule: when the earth receives seed, or the sea a ship, or another vessel in which food is placed, or something that has been deposited, or something that has been kept,
these things perish, but those that received them remain. With us, however, it was not so.
Rather, we who received the law and sinned perish along with our heart, which received it.
But your law does not perish; it endures in its glory.

While I was saying these things in my heart, I raised my eyes and saw a woman on my right, shaking and weeping aloud. She was sighing inwardly and was deeply distressed. Her clothes were torn, and dust lay on her head.
I left the thoughts I had been thinking, turned toward her, and said to her:
Why are you weeping and so distressed within yourself?
She answered me, “Leave me alone, my lord, so that I may weep for myself and go on sighing, because my soul is very bitter, and I am deeply humbled.”
I said to her, “Tell me what has happened to you.” She answered me:
I, your servant, was barren and bore no children, though I had lived with my husband for thirty years.
Every day and every hour throughout these thirty years, I kept praying and pleading with the Most High, day and night.

After these thirty years, God heard the voice of your servant and saw her lowliness. He looked upon my afflictions and gave me a son. I rejoiced and took great delight in him, together with my husband and all the people of my city, and we praised the Mighty One.
I raised him with great toil.
When he grew up, I set about finding him a wife, and I held a day of feasting and great celebration.
But when my son entered his bridal chamber, he fell down and died.
I overturned the lamps, and all the people of my city came forward to comfort me. I remained quiet until the next day and until night.
After they had all fallen asleep, thinking that I too was asleep, I got up in the night and fled. I came to this plain, as you now see.
I intend never to enter the city again, but to remain here, neither eating nor drinking, continually mourning and fasting until I die.
Then I put aside the thoughts I had been thinking, and answered her angrily:
You are more foolish than all other women! Do you not see our mourning and what has happened to us?
Look, Zion, the mother of us all, is in great distress and has been deeply humiliated.
But now mourning is called for; we are all mourning. You grieve for one son, but we, the whole world, grieve for our mother.
Ask the earth, and she will tell you, for she ought to mourn, because so many have lived upon her.
From the beginning, all those who have lived upon her, and the others who are coming—look, they are all going to destruction, and their multitude is destined for ruin.
Who, then, ought to mourn more: she who has lost this entire multitude, or you, who mourn for one?
But if you say to me, “My mourning is not like the earth’s, because I have lost the fruit of my womb, whom I bore in labor pains and raised in suffering,”
For the multitude has gone to the earth according to the earth’s nature, just as it came to it. But I say to you again:
Just as you gave birth with pain, so the earth too has given its fruit—humankind—from the beginning to the one who made it.
Now, then, contain your grief within yourself, and bear with strength the misfortune that has happened to you.
For if you acknowledge the justice of the Most High’s sentence, you too will receive your son back in time, and you will be praised among women.
“Go, then, into the city to your husband.” And she answered me:
I will not do that, and I will not enter the city or return to my husband. Instead, I will die here.
I spoke to her again and said:
No, woman! No, woman! Do not do such a thing. Instead, accept Zion’s calamity and take comfort in Jerusalem’s suffering,
For you have seen our sanctuaries laid waste, our altars overturned, and our temple demolished.

and in our worship, which has ceased; our praise, which has been taken away; our pride, which has fallen; the light of our lampstand, which has gone out; the ark of the covenant, which has been seized; our holy things, which have been defiled; the name we bear, which has been profaned; our freeborn people, who have been disgraced; our priests, who have been burned in fire; our Levites, who have been taken captive; our virgins, who have been defiled; our women, who have been forcibly violated; our seers, who have been seized; our righteous people, who have been scattered; our young men, who have been enslaved; and our mighty men, who have been weakened.
And greater than all these is what has happened to Zion’s seal: the seal of her glory has now been taken away, and she has been handed over to those who hate us.
So cast off your many sorrows, so that the Mighty One may be reconciled to you and the Most High may relieve you of the pains of your suffering.

While I was speaking with her, her face began to shine very brightly, and the appearance of her face became like lightning. I was very afraid to approach her, and my heart was utterly astonished. As I was wondering what this vision was,
she suddenly cried out in a loud and terrifying voice, so that the whole earth shook at her voice.
I looked, and there was no longer a woman visible to me, but a city being built. A place appeared, as though rising from enormous foundations. I was afraid and cried out in a loud voice, saying:
Where is the angel Uriel, who came to me on the first day? For he has brought me into this great terror. My end has become destruction, and my prayer a disgrace.
While I was still saying these things, lying on the ground like a dead man, the angel who had come to me before came to me and saw me
lying on the ground like a dead man, with my mind distraught. He took me by my right hand, strengthened me, and set me on my feet. He said to me:
What is wrong with you? Why are you trembling? Why have your thoughts and the understanding of your heart become confused? And I said to him:
Because you abandoned me! I did as you told me and went out to the plain. And now I have seen, and am still seeing, something I cannot explain. He answered and said to me:
“Stand on your feet, and I will explain it to you.” And I said to him,
“Speak, my lord. Only do not abandon me, so that I do not die before my time.
For I have seen something I did not know, and I am hearing something I do not understand.
Or perhaps my mind is deceiving me, and my soul is seeing a dream.
But now I ask you, my lord: explain this terrifying vision to your servant.”
He answered and said to me: Listen to me, and I will teach you. I will explain to you the things you are afraid of, for the Most High has revealed many mysteries to you.
For he has seen your integrity: you are deeply distressed over your people, you mourn greatly over your people, and you mourn greatly over Zion.
This, then, is the meaning: that woman who appeared to you a little while ago,
who was mourning, and whom you began to comfort,
now no longer appears to you as a woman, but has appeared to you as a city being built.
And as for what she was telling you about her son’s misfortune, this is the explanation:
The woman you saw is Zion, which you now see as a city being built.
As for what she told you about herself, that she had been barren for thirty years: this was because she had existed in the world for three thousand years without any offering being presented in her.
After three thousand years, Solomon built the city and presented an offering in her. That was when the barren woman gave birth to a son.
And when she told you that she had raised him in the world, this was the time when Jerusalem was inhabited.
And when she told you, ‘My son entered his bridal chamber and died,’ this is the downfall and calamity of Jerusalem.
You saw her likeness, how she was mourning over her children, and you began to comfort her about what had happened to her.
Now the Most High has seen that you are distressed with all your soul and that you grieve over her with all your heart. He has shown you the light of her glory and the beauty of her splendor.
For this reason I told you to wait for me in the plain, where no house had been built.
For I knew that the Most High was going to show you all these things.
For this reason I told you to come to a place where there is no foundation of a building.
For no human work could remain in the place where the city of the Most High was to be revealed.
But do not be afraid, and do not let your heart tremble. Instead, go in and see the light of her glory and the greatness of her buildings, as far as your eyes are able to see.
And after this you will hear as much as your ears are able to hear.
For you have been blessed more than many, and you have been named before the Most High among the few.
But tomorrow night you are to remain here.
And the Most High will show you a vision revealing what the Most High will do to the inhabitants of the earth in the last days.
And I slept there another night, as he had commanded me.
On the second night I saw a vision: an enormously large eagle was rising from the sea. It had twelve wings and three heads.
I looked, and it spread its wings over the whole earth. All the winds of heaven were blowing toward it, and the clouds were gathering around it.
And I saw thin, slender, small wings growing out of its wings.
Its heads were resting. The middle head was larger than the others, but it too was resting with them.
And I looked, and the eagle commanded its wings to rule over the whole earth and its inhabitants.
I saw how everything under heaven was subject to it, and none of the creatures on earth resisted it.
I looked, and there was the eagle, standing on its talons. It called out to its wings and said to them, “Go, rule over the whole earth. But now rest.
Do not seek to wake up all together. Instead, sleep, each of you in its own place, and wake up in turn.”
“But let the heads be kept for the end.”
And I saw that its voice did not come from its heads, but from the middle of its body.
And I counted its small wings, and there were eight of them.
And I looked, and one wing rose up on the right side and ruled over the whole earth.
I saw that its end came and it was destroyed, so that not even its place could be recognized. Then I looked, and there arose a second wing, and it too ruled over the whole earth for a long time.
And after it had ruled, its end came, and it was destroyed like the first.
And a voice was heard speaking to it:
“Listen, you who have held the earth all this time. Receive this message before you are destroyed.”
None of those who come after you will hold it for so long, not even for half that time.”
I looked, and there arose a third wing. It too ruled over the whole earth, like its former companions, and it too was destroyed like the earlier ones.
And this happened to all the wings: each of them ruled in turn and then was destroyed.
I looked, and at one point the small wings also arose on the right side to take possession of the earth. Some of them did take possession of it, but they were quickly destroyed.
Some of them rose but did not gain power.
And I looked after these things, and its twelve wings had been destroyed, along with two of the small wings.
Nothing remained of the eagle’s body except its three resting heads and six small wings.
I looked, and two wings separated from the small wings and went and stood beneath the head on the right side. The other four remained in their place.
And I looked, and those four small wings were planning to rise and take power.
And I looked, and one rose, but it was quickly destroyed.
Then a second rose, but it too was destroyed, even more quickly than the first.
I looked, and those two that remained among them were themselves planning to take power.
While they were planning to rule over the earth, I looked, and one of the resting heads—the middle one—awoke. It was larger than the other two heads.
[?] the two of them with it.
Together with the two that were with it, it turned and devoured the two small wings that were planning to rule.
That head took possession of the whole earth and oppressed its inhabitants with great hardship. It exercised greater power over the world than all the wings that had come before.
After this I looked, and suddenly that middle head was also destroyed, just as the wings had been.
But two heads remained, and they too ruled over the whole earth and its inhabitants.
And I looked, and the head on the right side devoured the one on the left.
And I heard a voice saying to me, “Look ahead of you, Ezra, and see what outcome you see.”
I looked, and there was something like a lion roused from the forest, crying out and roaring. I heard it address the eagle in a human voice, speaking and saying to it:
“Listen, eagle, and I will speak to you. The Most High says to you:”
“Are you not the one that remained of the four beasts that I had made to rule over my world, so that through them the times would reach their end?

You came fourth and defeated all the beasts that had gone before. You exercised power over the world with great hardship, and over the whole earth with bitter oppression. You lived in the world deceitfully for a long time.
And you judged the earth unjustly.

For you plundered and robbed the humble and the faithful. You mistreated the meek, hated the upright, and loved liars. You demolished the strongholds of the prosperous and brought down the walls of those who had not provoked you.
Your insolence rose up to the Most High, to the Mighty One.
The Most High looked at his times, and behold, they were complete, and his ages had reached their fulfillment.
Therefore you will surely be destroyed, eagle—you and your lofty wings, your small and wicked wings, your cruel heads, your evil talons, and your whole hateful, wicked body—
so that the whole earth may rest and find relief once it has been freed from oppression, as it awaits the judgment and mercy of its Maker.”
While the lion was speaking these words to the eagle, I looked.
Suddenly the remaining head was destroyed. Then the two wings that had gone over to it arose to rule, and their rule would come to an end and be full of turmoil.
I saw that they too were destroyed, and the eagle’s whole body was burning. The earth was greatly astonished. I awoke, trembling violently and in great fear, and said to myself:
For you have done all these things to me because you investigate the ways of the Most High.
“Here I am, falling apart within myself, and my spirit has grown very weak. Not even a little strength remains in me because of the great terror I experienced this night.”
And now I will ask the Most High to strengthen me to the end.
I said, “O Lord, my Lord, if I have found mercy in your eyes, and if I truly have greater favor with you than many others, and if my prayer has truly risen before your majestic presence,
Strengthen me and make known to me, your servant, the meaning and interpretation of this vision that I have seen, for my soul longs deeply for it.
For it is not because I am worthy that you have considered me fit to have the end of the times and the conclusion of the ages revealed to me.” He answered and said to me:
“This is the interpretation of the vision that you saw.
“The eagle that you saw rising from the sea is the fourth kingdom that appeared in a vision to your brother Daniel.
But it was not explained to him as I am explaining it to you now, or as I have explained it to you.
Look, days are coming when a kingdom will arise on the earth, and it will be more terrifying than all the kingdoms that came before it.
Twelve kings will reign in it, one after another.
But when the second reigns, he will hold power longer than those twelve.
This is the interpretation of the twelve wings that you saw.
As for your seeing a voice speaking, which came not from the eagle’s head but from the middle of its body,
this is its meaning: during the time of that kingdom there will be many divisions, and it will be in danger of falling. But it will not fall then; instead, it will be restored to its former rule.
And as for your seeing eight small wings that grew beneath its wings:
This is its meaning: eight kings will arise in it, whose times will be short and whose periods of rule will pass quickly. Two of them will perish
when the time comes for it to be divided. Four will be kept for a time, until the time comes for it to end, while two will be kept until the end.
And as for your seeing three heads on it that were at rest:
This is its meaning: at the end of the times, the Most High will raise up three kings. They will make many changes in it and crush the earth
and its inhabitants with great hardship, more than all those who came before them. For this reason they were called the eagle’s heads.
For they are the ones who renew its wickedness, and they will bring it to its end.
As for your seeing that one great head perish, it is because one of them will die in his own bed, though he too will suffer torment.
But the sword will devour the two who remain.
For the sword of one will devour his companion, but he too will fall by the sword in the end.
And because you saw two wings go to the head on the right side:
This is its meaning: these are the ones whom the Most High has set apart for its end. Their kingdom will come to an end, and it will be full of turmoil,
as you saw. As for your seeing a lion roused from the forest, crying out and roaring and speaking to the eagle, rebuking it for its injustice, with all the words that you heard:

this is the Messiah, whom the Most High has kept for the end of days, who will arise from David’s offspring. He will come and speak with them, rebuke them for their wickedness, reprove them for their wrongdoing, and lay their injustice before them.
For he will bring them alive before me for their judgment, and after he has rebuked them, he will destroy them.
But he will mercifully deliver the remnant of my people, those who have remained within my borders. He will give them joy until the end comes, the day of judgment about which I spoke with you before.
This is the vision you saw, and this is its interpretation.
You alone have been found worthy to know the mystery of the Most High.
Therefore write in a book all these things that you have seen, and put them in a hidden place.
Teach these things to the wise among your people, those you know whose hearts are able to hold and keep these mysteries.
But you must wait here another seven days, so that what the Most High wishes to reveal to you may be revealed to you.”
Then he left me. When the people saw that seven days had passed and I had not returned to the city, all the people gathered, from the least to the greatest. They set out and came to me and said:
How have we sinned against you, or what harm have we done you, that you have left us and settled here?
“You alone of all the prophets have been left to us, like a cluster of grapes after the harvest, like a lamp in a dark place, and like a safe harbor for a ship caught in a storm.
Are the calamities that have befallen us not enough for us, that you too should leave us?
If you are leaving us, it would have been better for us if we too had burned when Zion burned.
For we are no better off than those who died there.” Then I wept aloud and answered them:
Take courage, Israel, and do not grieve, house of Jacob.
For you are remembered before the Most High, and the Mighty One will never forget you.
“I have not abandoned you, and I will not abandon you. Rather, I came to this place to plead over Zion’s destruction and to ask for mercy over the humiliation of our sanctuary.”
And now, go, everyone to his own home. I will come to you after these days.
The people went to the city, as I had told them.
I stayed in the plain for seven days, as he had commanded me. I ate only the flowers of the field, and roots were my food during those days.
After seven days, I saw a vision in the night.
And look, a great wind arose in the sea, stirring up all its waves.

I looked, and that wind brought up from the heart of the sea something resembling a human being. I looked, and that man was flying with the clouds of heaven. Wherever he turned his face to look and see, everything trembled before his gaze.
Wherever the voice from his mouth reached, all who heard his voice melted, as wax melts when fire heats it.
After these things I looked, and there was an innumerable multitude of people gathered from the four winds of heaven to wage war against the man who had come up from the sea.
I saw that he cut out a high mountain for himself, flew up, and stood on it.
I tried to see the region or place from which that mountain had been cut out, but I could not.
After these things I looked, and all those who had gathered to wage war against him were very afraid. Nevertheless, they dared to wage war.
When he saw the onrush of their approaching multitude, he did not raise his hand. He was not holding a spear or any weapon of war. But I saw

how he sent out something like waves of fire from his mouth alone, a flaming breath from his lips, and stormy embers from his tongue. All these mingled together: the waves of fire, the flaming breath, and the great storm.

They fell upon the onrush of that approaching multitude, which was ready to fight, and suddenly burned them all up. Nothing could be seen of that innumerable crowd except the dust of ashes and the smell of smoke. I looked and was amazed.
After these things I saw that man come down from that mountain, and he was calling another great, peaceful crowd to himself.

Figures of many people were approaching him. Some were joyful, some were sorrowful, some were bound, and some were bringing those who were approaching. I awoke because of my great trembling. I appealed to the Most High and said:
“You are the one who from the beginning showed your servant these wonders. Though I am unworthy, you considered me worthy to have my petition accepted.
Now reveal to me also the interpretation of this vision.
For as I consider it in my mind, woe to those who survive in those days, and far greater woe to those who do not survive!
For because they did not survive, they will be distressed
As for what is reserved for those who survive in the last days, they themselves do not attain it—not even those who have survived [?].
For this reason, woe! For they see great dangers together with many afflictions, as these visions show.
Nevertheless, it is better for someone to stand amid danger and encounter these things than to pass from the world like a cloud and not see what happens at the end of the ages.”
And he answered and said to me, “I will also tell you the interpretation of your vision, and I will reveal to you the things you spoke about.”
As for what you said about those who survive and those who do not survive, this is the answer:
