The one who endures danger at that time is the one who protects those who are exposed to danger, those who have deeds and faith toward the Most High and Mighty One.
See, then, that greater blessedness has been given to those who survive than to those who have died.
Now this is the interpretation of your vision: As for your seeing a man coming up from the heart of the sea,
He is the one whom the Most High has kept for many ages, through whom he will deliver his creation, and he will bring those who remain through.
And as for your seeing a blast of fire and storm coming out of his mouth,
As for his holding neither a spear nor a weapon of war in his hand, yet destroying the approaching multitude of that crowd which came to wage war against him, this is the meaning:
Look, the days are coming when the Most High will act to deliver those on the earth.
Great confusion will come upon the inhabitants of the earth.
They will plan to wage war against one another: city against city, region against region, people against people, and kingdom against kingdom.
When these signs that I have already told you about occur, then my Son will be revealed, whom you saw as a man coming up.
When all the nations hear his voice, each of them will leave his own land and abandon the warfare among them.
An innumerable crowd will gather together, as you saw, wishing to come and wage war against that man.
But he will stand on the summit of Mount Zion.
Zion will come and be revealed to everyone, prepared and built, just as you saw the mountain cut out without hands.

My Son will rebuke these nations that have come because of their wickedness, which were likened to the storm. He will set before them their evil deeds and the torment with which they are to be tormented.
Afterward, what was likened to the flame will destroy them without effort, through his law, which was likened to fire.
And as for your seeing him calling and gathering to himself another great, peaceful crowd,

They are the nine and a half tribes that were taken captive from their land in the days of King Josiah, whom Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, took captive. He brought them across the Euphrates River, and they were carried captive to another land.
For they had considered the matter among themselves and agreed on this plan: to leave the multitude of nations and go to an interior region where no human race had ever lived.
so that at least there they might keep their law, which they had not kept in their own land.
They entered through the narrow passages of the Euphrates.
For the Most High performed wonders for them then: he held back the outlets of the river until they had all crossed.
But for them to travel overland, there was a long journey to make—a journey of a year and a half. That region is called Arzaph, the end of the world.
They lived there until the last time. And then, when they are to come again,
Again the Most High will hold back the outlets of the River Euphrates so that they can cross. That is why you saw the great crowd gathering in peace.
But those who remain of your people will also live, those who are found within my holy boundaries.
And when he destroys the multitude of nations that have gathered, he will shelter the people who remain.
Then he will show them still greater wonders.
And I spoke to him again: “O Lord, my lord, explain this to me: Why did I see the man coming up from the heart of the sea?” And he answered me:
“Just as no one can search out and discover or know what is in the depths of the sea, so no one among those on earth can see my son or those with him, except at that time, on his day.
This is the interpretation of the vision you saw. For this reason these things have been revealed to you—to you alone—
Because you have set aside your own concerns and have concerned yourself with mine, and have sought the things of the law,
For you have guided your life with wisdom and called understanding ‘my mother.’
I have therefore shown you these things, for a reward awaits with the Most High. After three days I will speak with you about other things and explain other wonders to you.”
And I went and walked about a great deal in the plain, praising and thanking the Most High for the wonders he performed from time to time.
and because he governs the times and what happens in them. I stayed there for three days.
After these things, while I was sitting beneath an oak,
Then a voice came from the bush opposite me and said to me, “Ezra, Ezra!” I said, “Here I am,” and stood on my feet. And he said to me:
I revealed myself from the bush and spoke with Moses when my people were enslaved in Egypt.
“I sent him, and he brought my people out of Egypt and led them into the wilderness. I brought him up Mount Sinai and kept him with me for many days.
I explained many wonders to him, made known to him the mysteries of the times, and showed him the completion of the ages. And I commanded him, saying:
‘Of these words, you must conceal some and reveal others.’
And now I say to you, Ezra:
“Keep in your heart and conceal the signs I showed you earlier, the visions you saw, and their interpretation, which you heard.
For you are being taken away from humanity, and from now on you will be with my son and with those like you until the times are completed.
For the world has lost its youth, and the times are approaching old age.
Now, therefore, put your household in order, admonish your people, comfort their humble ones, and instruct their wise ones. Leave behind now this perishable life.
Remove from yourself the burden of humanity, cast away thoughts of death, and strip off now your weak nature. Set aside these thoughts that trouble you, and hurry to depart from these times.
For after the evils you have seen happening now, still worse ones will follow.
For as the world dwindles in its old age, evils increase upon the inhabitants of the earth.
For truth is withdrawing further and further, and falsehood is drawing near. Already the eagle you saw in the vision is hurrying to come.”
I answered and said, “Let me speak before you, Lord.
“I am going, as you commanded me, and I will admonish this people now living. But who will admonish those yet to be born?
For the world lies in darkness, and its inhabitants have no light.
For your law has been burned, and no one knows the deeds you have done or what you are going to do.

If, then, I have found favor before you, my Lord, place the Holy Spirit within me, and I will write everything that has happened in the world from the beginning, everything that was written in your law, so that people may be able to find the path, and those who wish to live at the end may know the way.”
He answered me, “Go, gather your people, and tell them not to look for you for forty days.
Prepare many writing tablets for yourself, and take with you Seraiah, Dariah, Shelemiah, Elkanah, and Shiel—these five men, because they are skilled at writing quickly.
Then come here, and I will light a lamp of understanding in your heart that will not go out until you finish what you are to write.
When you have finished, make some of them public, but keep others hidden and hand them over to the wise. For tomorrow at this time you will begin to write.”
I went as he had commanded me, gathered all the people, and said to them,
“Israel, listen to these words.
Long ago our ancestors lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt, and they were delivered from there.
They received the law of life but did not keep it. You too, after them, have transgressed it.
“Land was given to you as an inheritance in the land of Zion. But you and your ancestors acted wickedly and did not keep the ways that Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded you.
So the Most High, who is a just judge, took away from you what had been given to you for a time.
Now you are here in distress, and your brothers are farther inland, in another land.
If, then, you admonish yourselves and discipline your hearts, you will be preserved during your lives, and after death mercy will be shown to you.
For judgment comes after death, when we live again. Then the name of the righteous will be revealed, and the deeds of the wicked will be seen.”
But let no one approach me, and do not look for me for forty days.”
I took these five men, as he had commanded me, and went to the plain. We remained there, as he had told me.
The next day, a voice called to me and said, “Ezra, Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I give you to drink.”
I opened my mouth and saw [?] a full cup was there for me. It was filled with something like water, but its appearance was like fire.
I took it and drank. As I drank it, my heart welled up with understanding, my breast poured forth wisdom, and my spirit retained its memory.
My mouth was opened and was not shut.

The Most High gave understanding to those five men, and they wrote down what was spoken in succession, using written characters they did not know. I stayed there forty days. They wrote during the day,
and at night they ate only bread. I spoke during the day, and at night I did not stop.
During those forty days, ninety-four books were written.

When the forty days were completed, the Most High spoke with me and said to me, “Make public these twenty-four books that you wrote first, and let both the worthy and the unworthy among the people read them.”
But keep these seventy and hand them over to the wise among your people.
For in them are the channels of understanding, the springs of wisdom, and the light of knowledge.”

I did so, in the seventh year of the sixth week, after five thousand years from creation, and three months and twelve days. At that time Ezra was caught up and taken to the place of those who were like him, after he had written all these things. He was called the scribe of the knowledge of the Most High forever and ever. The first discourse of Ezra is finished.
